correctness.rationale: Reconstructed assumptions, quantifiers, force normalizations, excluded endpoints, and impact geometry. The radial-force limit \(\rho\ddot\rho\to-2G\sigma(x_*)\) yields \(\dot\rho^2\sim4G\sigma(x_*)\log(1/\rho)\). Cancellation under \(C^1\) regularity gives \(\ddot x=2G\sigma'(x_*)\log(1/\rho)+o(\log(1/\rho))\), integrable in collision time, hence finite terminal axial speed. The potential has finite part \(B_*\), by uniform dominated convergence; energy yields \(\dot\rho^2=A\log(1/\rho)+2H+2GB_*-v_*^2+o(1)\). Direct integration gives the second-order relative clock correction \(-(1+C/A)/(2L)\). Two integrations give the axial impulse and position limits. Exact linear-density formulas agree with quadrature at four points and the trajectory check supports them at four radii; finite calculations alone do not prove the limits.

originality.rationale: Compared actual implications: arXiv:2611.08625v1 Theorem 5.5 supplies only the radial force and incidence limits, while its §5.1 gives one-sided clock bounds. The present impact theorem adds a nonlocal exact potential finite part, an O(1) radial kinetic normalization, second-order collision time, and density-gradient axial impulse and displacement for all positive C1 densities at interior impacts. The earlier AAS 24-333 paper treats linear densities and relative equilibria/collision questions, not these displayed asymptotics. value.rationale: At an interior collision the rod-induced logarithmic singularity controls the observable remaining flight time and local axial velocity. The leading source result leaves the second-order clock and tangential impulse undetermined. The finite-part potential reveals global density information at O(1) in the transverse kinetic scale, whereas the tangential impulse identifies local density slope; such a separation is nontrivial for inhomogeneous gravitating rods and potentially useful for collision regularization/inverse diagnostics. Not a generic textbook substitution or an arbitrary parameter slice.
